# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-2 (Extended v37)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod attendance); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); **1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion and Bombarda's restaurant dinner); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop with Thénardier family and Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's Champmathieu revelation; Valjean's crisis and journey planning); 1862 (narrative reflection on changed Paris)**; present day (spring transitioning to late August/early September, England); future wedding (following spring); 1795 (Jean Valjean's theft at Faverolles and trial)
- Primary locations: M. sur M. (industrial center, upper and lower town divisions, factory, hospital, infirmary for workmen, schools, dispensary, free school for infants, industrial exhibition venue, officers' café, police station, parsonage); Montfermeil (Thénardier cook-shop, Boulanger Lane); England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford harbor towns, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby); Secondary locations: San Francisco, New York, Eastern Prussia, Germany, Hamburgh, Paris, Italy, Durance, Château-Arnoux, Senez, Briançon, Aix, Draguignan, Embrun, Chastelar, Arche, Barcelonette, Jauziers, Tuiles, Joug-de-l'Aigle, Ubaye, Ubayette, Ollioules, Nice, Piédmont, Couloubrieux, Cannes, Rue Cassette, Elmhaven, Staveford, Grenoble, Bras d'Asse, Escoublon, Grasse, Franche-Comté, Pontarlier, Lods, Châtillon, Audincourt, Beure, Faverolles, Brie, Tottlingen, Toulon, Quenford, Ravenmere, Basses-Alpes, Latin Quarter Paris, Mount Sainte-Geneviève, Toulouse, Cahors, Limoges, Montauban, Naples, Saint-Cloud, Fécamp, Vanvres, Issy, Passy, l'Étoile, Champs-Élysées, Rue de Rivoli, Delorme Alley, Place de la Concorde, Place Louis XV, Avenue de Neuilly, Tuileries, Marigny square, Odéon, Luxembourg, Rue Madame, Allée de l'Observatoire, Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas, Coural das Freiras vineyard, Madeira, Rue Saint-Antoine Paris, Arras, Pont-à-Mousson, Ailly-le-Haut-Clocher, Rue Saint-Saulve, Rue Montre-de-Champigny, Rue Guibourg, Rue du Garraud-Blanc, Marines near Pontoise, D——, Manosque, Sisteron, Hautes-Alpes, Lower Boulonnais
- **Recurring atmospheric descriptions (M. sur M./Montfermeil, 1818-1823)**: Evening at cook-shop; bell for vespers rings thinly; children chase hoop shrieking; bees hum in lavender behind parsonage; chalked crooked sun on forge wall; cart with turnips creaks past well; gulls quarrel over fish heads; dog barks then goes quiet; frost silvered hedges overnight; light went early; road rutted and puddled after thaw; wind off water with salt and tar smell; smoke from chimneys lay flat over fields; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; rain threatening since morning but held off

## Main Characters and Relationships

**M. Charles Myriel / Monseigneur Bienvenu (Bishop)—DECEASED by 1821**
- French aristocrat; family ruined by Revolution; emigrated to Italy; wife died. Became priest, then Bishop of D——; encountered Napoleon circa coronation epoch.
- Redistributed entire 15,000 franc yearly State salary across 23 charitable categories; retained 1,500 francs yearly for sustenance.
- Philosophy: society culpable for poverty and ignorance; strove to dress wounds and relieve suffering.
- 1815 (October evening): Warmly accepted Valjean at supper; explained fruitières of Pontarlier. At parting (before theft): told Valjean "You have promised me to become an honest man. I buy your soul. I take it away from the spirit of perversity; I give it to the good God."
- **Spiritual impact on Valjean**: Following theft and mystical crisis, Valjean confronted conscience through Bishop's radiance; mystical vision marked decisive transformation through divine confrontation with virtue's radiance.
- Death by 1821. Upon news, Madeleine entered visible mourning; gossip concluded Madeleine was Bishop's relative, raising his credit greatly in noble circles of M. sur M.

**Jean Valjean / Father Madeleine—ACUTE CRISIS (Late January 1823)**
- **Background**: Poor peasant of Brie; became tree-pruner at Faverolles. At 25-26 (1795): condemned to five years galleys for stealing loaf; sentence extended to nineteen years total for four escape attempts.
- **Toulon (19 years)**: Became number 24,601; effaced identity; recognized society culpable for poverty; at age 40 learned to read, write, cipher.
- **Liberation**: Upon release, received yellow passport; calculated wrongful earnings reduction; worked at orange-flower distillery at Grasse before arriving D——, October 1815.
- **October 1815 arrival at D——**: Medium stature, robust, ~46 years old; burned/tanned face; worn blue drilling trousers, patched blouse, iron-shod shoes, shaved head, long beard; packed knapsack, enormous knotty stick. At supper: overwhelmed by acceptance, exclaimed about not being driven forth, being called "sir," sheets.
- **Theft and spiritual crisis (October 1815)**: Seized silver, fled. Post-theft, three leagues from D——: robbed Little Gervais of forty sous. Psychological crisis: Bishop's pardon eclipsed self-image. **Mystical vision**: Conscience weighed Bishop and Valjean; Bishop grew resplendent while Valjean vanished; only Bishop remained filling whole soul with magnificent radiance. Wept as past life recurred with unprecedented clarity; perceived Satan by light of Paradise. **Crisis marked decisive transformation through divine confrontation with virtue's radiance.**
- **Subsequent escape and reinvention**: Disappeared, sold Bishop's silver (reserved candlesticks as souvenir), crept town to town across France. Arrived M. sur M., established as Father Madeleine (late 1815 onward). Fire incident on entry: rushed into flames, saved two children, gendarmes forgot to demand passport.
- **Manufacturing innovation (late 1815 onward)**: Substituted gum-lac for resin in black goods production; used sheet-iron slides simply laid together instead of soldered. Within three years: became rich, enriched town. By 1820: possessed 630,000-640,000 francs with Laffitte (before spending >1,000,000 for town and poor).
- **Charitable works**: Founded six hospital beds; constructed two schools (girls and boys); allotted salary from own funds to instructors; created infant school; established fund aiding old and infirm workmen; established free dispensary; established infirmary for workmen in factory building itself, served by two sisters of charity.
- **Political honors (1819-1820)**: 1819: King appointed mayor; refused. 1819: Products exhibited industrially; King appointed chevalier Legion of Honor; refused cross. 1820: King reappointed mayor; after old woman questioned refusal angrily, irritated into accepting.
- **Personal character (1820-1821)**: Remained simple; gray hair, serious eye, sunburned complexion, thoughtful visage. Wore wide-brimmed hat, long coat buttoned to chin. Took meals alone with open book; possessed well-selected little library. Language grew polished and gentle. Prodigiously strong. Pockets full going out, empty returning. Taught peasants useful secrets. **Performed multitude of good actions concealing agency**: penetrated houses privately at night, forced doors during absences, left pieces of gold forgotten on furniture.
- **Civic veneration (1815-1821)**: Blackening and calumnies initially subsided through ill-nature's disappearance to universal respect. By 1821, word "Monsieur le Maire" pronounced with almost same accent as "Monseigneur the Bishop" had been in D——. People consulted him from ten leagues around; put end to differences, prevented lawsuits, reconciled enemies.
- **January 1823 incident with Fantine and subsequent crisis**: Upon news of Fantine's arrest and street altercation, Madeleine arrived at police station. When Fantine saw him, she rose crying out, spit in his face. Madeleine calmly wiped his face and ordered her release. **Subsequent dialogue with Javert**: Explained he was passing square, learned "townsman was in the wrong." Javert resisted; Madeleine's command for release was immediately obeyed. **Redemptive promise to Fantine**: "I have heard you... I will pay your debts, I will send for your child... You have never ceased to be virtuous and holy in the sight of God."
- **That same night after police station**: Javert wrote letter to Paris addressed to Monsieur Chabouillet, Secretary of Préfet of Police; posted it himself next morning.
- **ACUTE CRISIS (Late January 1823, following Javert's revelation)**: Upon Javert's articulation of name Champmathieu, Valjean struck with stupor; felt shudder preceding great shocks; bent like oak before storm. First instinct: go, run, denounce himself, take Champmathieu from prison, place himself there—"as painful and as poignant as an incision in living flesh." Then thought: "We will see! We will see!" Repressed generous instinct; recoiled before heroism. **Initial response**: Carried away by instinct of self-preservation; rallied ideas in haste, stifled emotions, took Javert's presence into consideration as great danger, postponed all decision with firmness of terror, resumed calmness as warrior picks up buckler.
- **State during rest of day**: Whirlwind within, profound tranquility without. Took no preservative measures. Everything confused and jostling in brain. Trouble so great could not perceive single idea distinctly.
- **Behavior towards Fantine and preparation**: Repaired to Fantine's bed as usual, prolonged visit through kindly instinct, told himself must behave thus and recommend her well to sisters "in case he should be obliged to be absent himself." Vague feeling he might be obliged to go to Arras. Without having made up mind to trip, said to himself that being beyond shadow of suspicion, nothing out of way in being witness to what would take place. **Engaged tilbury from Scaufflaire to be prepared in any event.**
- **Evening meditation**: Deluded himself at first with feeling of security and solitude; bolt drawn, thought himself impregnable; candle extinguished, felt invisible. Then took possession of himself; set elbows on table, leaned head on hand, began to meditate in dark.
- **Meditative crisis deepens**: Questioned himself: "Where do I stand? Am not I dreaming? What have I heard? Is it really true that I have seen that Javert? Who can that Champmathieu be? So he resembles me! Is it possible?" Gradually vague outlines took form in meditation; began recognizing fact that, critical and extraordinary as situation was, he was completely master of it.
- **Consciousness of fate's logic**: Seemed to find himself slipping down declivity in middle of night, erect, shivering, on brink of abyss. Distinctly perceived in darkness stranger, man unknown, whom destiny had mistaken for him, thrusting into gulf in his stead. For gulf to close, someone—himself or other man—must fall; he had only let things take their course.
- **Recognition of inevitable substitution**: Light became complete; he acknowledged: His place empty in galleys but awaiting him; do what he would, still awaiting him; theft from little Gervais had led him back to it; vacant place would await him, draw him on until he filled it; inevitable and fatal. Then said to himself: At this moment, he had substitute; certain Champmathieu had that ill luck; being present in galleys in person of Champmathieu, present in society under name M. Madeleine, he had nothing more to fear, provided he did not prevent men from sealing over head of Champmathieu "this stone of infamy which, like stone of sepulchre, falls once, never to rise again."
- **Conscience convulsion**: Strange and violent movement—indescribable convulsion of conscience stirring up all doubtful in heart, composed of irony, joy, despair, called "outburst of inward laughter."
- **Internal dialogue**: After moment, resumed gloomy dialogue in which he who spoke and he who listened, saying that he preferred to ignore, listening to that he preferred not to hear, yielding to mysterious power which said: "Think!" as it said to condemned man two thousand years ago, "March on!"
- **Dual struggle**: Two ideas governing unhappy man engaged in serious struggle—to conceal his name and sanctify his life; to escape men and return to God. Occasionally these thoughts conflict; man whom country calls M. Madeleine sacrifices security to virtue. **CURRENT STATE**: Torn between self-preservation instinct (permitting Champmathieu substitution) and moral imperative to prevent innocent man's condemnation; journey to Arras/Montfermeil imminent; cottages of conscience facing final test.

**Javert** (Police Inspector at M. sur M., appointed circa 1815-1819)
- **Origin and psychology**: Born in prison; mother fortune-teller, father in galleys. Conscious of rigidity, regularity, probity with inexpressible hatred for bohemians. Entered police; succeeded. At 40, appointed inspector at M. sur M.
- **Instinctual opposition to Madeleine**: One of few escaping "contagion" of respect for Madeleine. Possessed "bestial instinct" creating imperious antipathies.
- **Physical appearance**: Flat nose, enormous whiskers, rare terrible laugh, savage fold around nose, little skull with great jaw, hair concealing forehead, permanent central frown, obscure gaze, pursed terrible mouth, air of ferocious command.
- **Characteristic bearing**: Brow beneath hat, eyes beneath eyebrows, chin in cravat, hands in sleeves, cane under coat.
- **Recognition of Valjean identity and denunciation (late January 1823)**: **CLAIM/FACT**: Believes Madeleine is Jean Valjean, convict whom he knew as adjutant-guard at Toulon twenty years prior. **Evidence cited**: Resemblance; inquiries at Faverolles; strength; adventure with Fauchelevent; skill in marksmanship; slight leg drag. **Conviction and action**: Impelled by wrath, Javert denounced Madeleine to the Prefecture. **Claim about Valjean's history**: After leaving galleys, Valjean robbed bishop, committed theft with violence on public highway against little Savoyard; disappeared eight years ago.
- **Confrontation with Madeleine (late January 1823)**: Confronts Madeleine with grave, supplicating words in study. Was "unconsciously full of simplicity and dignity." Informs Madeleine of arrest of old fellow named Father Champmathieu near Ailly-le-Haut-Clocher, described as "very wretched creature"; arrested last autumn for theft of cider apples; wall scaled, branches broken; arrested still holding branch. **States**: "Up to this point it was merely an affair of a misdemeanor. But here is where Providence intervened." (Details of Providence's intervention not fully disclosed.)
- **Reaction to Madeleine's dismissal (late January 1823)**: Madeleine abruptly dismisses Javert's account, dispatching him on multiple minor official tasks: complaint against carter Pierre Chesnelong; gutter complaint of M. Charcellay; police regulation infractions verification (Rue Guibourg at Widow Doris's; Rue du Garraud-Blanc at Madame Renée le Bossé's). Madeleine inquires whether Javert will be absent, noting he mentioned trip to Arras in week or ten days.
- **Post-1820 response to mayoral authority**: Upon seeing Madeleine clothed in scarf of mayoral authority, felt shudder watch-dog might experience smelling wolf in master's clothes. From that time forth, avoided him as much as possible; when service imperatively demanded meeting, addressed him with profound respect.
- **January 1823 street incident and police station with Fantine**: Arrested Fantine following altercation with dandy (Monsieur Bamatabois). Dragged her to police station. Judged woman's crime serious: prostitute made attempt on citizen's life. Upon Madeleine's arrival and command for release, **experienced "intoxication of amazement"** exceeding all possible astonishment; thought and word failed equally. **Unspoken hideous comparison formed** concerning woman and mayor's relationship. When Madeleine explained townsman was wrong, **felt compelled to oppose mayor for first time in his life**; insisted matter within his police authority; declared would detain Fantine. **Madeleine's command to release Fantine immediately obeyed**, demonstrating absolute authority superseding Javert's protests.

**Fantine—MYSTICAL REDEMPTION ARC (Continuing)**
- **1817 status**: Beautiful, sunny hair; youngest grisette; radiant, perfumed; serenity of toil. In love with Félix Tholomyès.
- **1817 abandonment**: Tholomyès departed via Toulouse diligence; left her dazzled and alone.
- **1818 spring (Montfermeil arrival)**: Transformed, difficult to recognize. Pale, weary, sickly; golden hair concealed beneath ugly, tight, nun-like cap; eyes not dry for long. Placed child with Thénardiers; paid initial fee (50-57 francs).
- **Post-dismissal economic catastrophe (1818-1823)**: Attempted domestic service but no one would hire her. Learned sublime talent of indigence: live without fire in winter, save candles, subsist on less than sou. Winter cycle: short days, no warmth, no light, no noonday. Creditors harassed continuously. Thénardiers wrote claiming Cosette ill with miliary fever requiring expensive drugs; threatened Cosette's death if payments not sent within week. Sacrificed hair. By end, resigned, marble-like indifference.
- **January 1823 street incident and arrest**: Snowy evening, dandy (Monsieur Bamatabois) wore morillo and large cloak, smoking. Put snow down her back. Fantine struck out with feet and fists, bareheaded, howling, minus hair and teeth, livid with wrath. Officers applauded. Javert dragged her to police station.
- **At station**: Spoke rent in twain, shaken with sobs, blinded with tears, wringing hands. **"Great sorrow is a divine and terrible ray, which transfigures the unhappy. At that moment Fantine had become beautiful once more."** Kissed Javert's coat, tenderly pleading. Upon learning Madeleine was present, rose like spectre, thrust aside soldiers, gazed intently with bewildered air. She **spit in his face**. Madeleine calmly wiped his face and ordered her release.
- **Madeleine's redemptive promise (after release)**: Declared: "I will pay your debts, I will send for your child... You shall be honest and happy once more... You have never ceased to be virtuous and holy in the sight of God."
- **Fantine's response**: Stunned by vision of paradise; stared stupidly; gave vent to sobs.
- **Following day**: Madeleine standing at her bedside, gazing at crucifix with look full of pity, anguish, supplication. Addressed her: "You have suffered much, poor mother... this hell from which you have just emerged is the first form of heaven. It was necessary to begin there."
- **Medical condition and mystical redemption (post-January 1823)**: Sisters initially received woman with repugnance; within days Fantine disarmed them through humble, gentle speech; motherhood provoked tenderness. Amid fever, spoke: "I have been a sinner; but when I have my child beside me, it will be a sign that God has pardoned me... Cosette is an angel, my sisters." Did not recover health; condition became more grave week by week. Snow applied to bare skin between shoulder-blades caused sudden suppression of perspiration, violently developing malady smouldering for many years. Doctor examined chest, shook his head. **Consumption/tuberculosis progressing; Madeleine informed "is losing ground fast".**

**Cosette (Euphrasie)** (Age 1823: approximately 7-8 years old)
- **Appearance at arrival (1818 spring, age 2-3)**: Most divine creature; coquettish dress with fine linen cap, Valenciennes lace; admirably rosy and healthy; great blue eyes with magnificent lashes.
- **Subsequent treatment by Thénardiers (post-1818 onward)**: After mother's money spent, treated as charity case. Dressed in cast-off petticoats; fed on scraps; made to run on errands, sweep, wash dishes, carry burdens. Called the _Lark_ in neighborhood. Sweet, feeble being, incessantly punished, scolded, ill-used, beaten.
- **Thénardier's obstruction (late January 1823 onward — PLAN)**: Thénardier does not "let go of the child"; gives hundred insufficient reasons. Cosette not quite well enough to take journey in winter. Petty but pressing debts remain in neighborhood.

**Thénardier** (Cook-shop keeper at Montfermeil)
- Runs cook-shop in Montfermeil where Fantine placed Cosette (1818).
- **Financial scheme with Fantine**: Received initial payment (50-57 francs) for Cosette's care. First six months demanded seven francs monthly; then raised to twelve francs; then fifteen francs. Fantine became irregular in payments.
- **Fabricated medical claims (1818-1823)**: Wrote constantly claiming Cosette ill with miliary fever requiring expensive drugs; threatened Cosette's death if payments not sent within week.
- **Billing for false medical expenses (January 1823)**: Presented bill for five hundred and some odd francs to Madeleine. Included two items over three hundred francs—one for doctor, one for apothecary who attended Éponine and Azelma through two long illnesses. Cosette had not been ill; only "trifling substitution of names." Wrote at foot "Received on account, three hundred francs."

**Sister Perpétue** (Sisters of Charity at M. sur M. infirmary)
- Ordinary villager, sister of charity in coarse style. Robust nun from Marines near Pontoise; chattered patois, droned, grumbled; sugared potion according to bigotry or hypocrisy of invalid; treated patients abruptly, roughly; was crabbed with dying; was bold, honest, and ruddy.

**Sister Simplice** (Sisters of Charity at M. sur M. infirmary)
- Upon entrance into order, had two faults which she gradually corrected: taste for dainties and liking to receive letters. Never read anything but book of prayers printed in Latin in coarse type. Did not understand Latin but understood the book.

**Monsieur Scaufflaire** (Fleming, horse-trader of M. sur M.)
- Possesses small white horse from Lower Boulonnais; full of fire; originally thought to be vicious and saddle-horse unsuitable; now gentle as girl, harnessed to carriage. Prefers drawing to carrying/being mounted. **FACT**: Has rented tilbury (carriage) with white horse to Madeleine for journey (Valjean engaged it to be prepared in any event).

**Dandy of M. sur M. / Monsieur Bamatabois** (January 1823)
- Elector and proprietor of handsome three-story cut-stone house with balcony forming corner of esplanade.
- January 1823 incident: Wore morillo, large cloak, was smoking. Put snow down Fantine's back in ball-dress with neck uncovered and flowers in hair, in front of officers' café. Engaged in altercation; she struck out; officers applauded. **Javert's police report**: Dandy's "attempt on citizen's life" was ground for Fantine's arrest.

**Minor Characters**
- **Yera Stenworth**: By trade a shepherd; born in Ravenmere. (Context/role not yet disclosed in excerpts.)
- **Lurald Stenworth ("Lame Lurald")**: By trade a weaver. (Context/role not yet disclosed in excerpts.)
- **Yedan Corrford**: Worked as a tanner; born at Dunstead. (Context/role not yet disclosed in excerpts.)

## Themes
- **Redemptive mercy and transformative Christian charity**; power of acceptance restoring dignity
- **Divine pardon and mystical confrontation with virtue's radiance**; motherhood as mystical redemption; great sorrow as divine ray transfiguring unhappy
- **Authority hierarchy crisis**: Javert's absolute legal authority and discretionary police power confronted by Madeleine's mayoral command; systemic breakdown when administrative mercy supersedes police discretion
- **Javert's cognitive crisis and identity obsession**: Denunciation to Prefecture; confrontation with mayor; dismissal and dispatch on minor tasks to isolate him during crisis
- **Valjean's acute moral crisis (late January 1823)**: Self-preservation instinct warring with moral imperative; temptation to permit innocent substitution (Champmathieu for Valjean) vs. duty to prevent injustice; recognition of fate's logic (vacant galley place inexorably awaiting him); conscience convulsion between security and virtue; **imminent journey to Arras (trial site) or Montfermeil (Cosette retrieval) both forcing confrontation with destiny**
- **Fantine's spiritual and physical redemption arc**: Recovery of dignity through Madeleine's promise; transformation from marble resignation to mystical hope; sisters' recognition of her holiness; anticipated reunion with Cosette as sign of divine pardon; physical decline with consumption progressing fatally
- **Maternal love as redemptive theology**: Fantine's conviction that Cosette's innocent presence will manifest God's pardon; child as angel
- **Inmost recesses of soul as spectacle**: Narrative meditation on conscience as chaos, furnace, lair, pandemonium, battlefield; penetrating livid face of reflection reveals battles of giants, skirmishes of hydras, visionary circles; word as magnificent mystery passing between thought and conscience within man
